title: Tiered Commitment Flex-Play: HC & Pricing Sensitivity Matrix — Q1 2028
body:
Purpose:
Quick working sheet to evaluate a tiered/reserved-commitment pricing product (2T/4T/8T GPU months equivalent) and the headcount implications across sales, solutions, and infra for H1 2028. Focus is pricing elasticity vs. headcount flex (hire fast vs. hire slow) and a fallback play (burst-to-hosted) for demand shocks.

Executive summary (draft):
- We model 4 primary market scenarios for Q1–Q2 2028: Aggressive adoption, Conservative adoption, Hybrid tier shift, and Demand shock.
- Primary lever: offer tiered discounts for 12-month commitments; secondary lever: upfront vs. monthly billing cadence.
- Key question: what minimum committed revenue (and conversion) justifies 6 hires in Solutions vs. deferring to 2 FTEs + contractor network?

Assumptions (baseline):
- ASP (hosted equivalent) = $0.0026 / generation token unit (for comparability).
- Reserved SKU discount bands from baseline: 15% (2T), 28% (4T), 42% (8T) at 12-month commit.
body_extra:
- Gross margin on hosted (current): 60% after infra + SRE allocation. Reserved margin improves due to committed utilization (target 72% at 4T).
- Avg deal conversion time = 45 days (sales + legal cycle).
- Customer cohort lifetime = 24 months modeled for NPV in sensitivity.
- Hiring: ramp to headcount takes 8–10 weeks per new FTE; cost per new Solutions hire (fully loaded) = $220k/year; sales = $240k/year; infra/ops = $300k/year.

Scenario matrix (summary table):
Columns: Scenario | Market growth | Avg commit size | Conversion rate | HC hires recommended | Expected SRR (run-rate rev) delta
Rows:
1) Aggressive adoption | +35% YoY | 4T avg | 18% conversion | +6 solutions, +2 sales | +$3.2M SRR vs baseline
2) Conservative adoption | +6% YoY | 2T avg | 6% conversion | +1 solutions (temp contractor) | +$420k SRR
3) Hybrid tier shift | +18% YoY | mix 2T/4T | 11% conversion | +3 solutions, +1 infra | +$1.4M SRR
4) Demand shock (elasticity event) | -22% YoY | shift to monthly / hosted | 3% conversion | freeze hires, reroute to hosted burst | -$1.1M SRR

Headcount plan (H1 2028) — modeled as alternative hires: fast vs slow:
- Fast hire (target to hit Aggressive): Solutions +6 (Jan–Mar), Sales +2 (Feb–Apr), Infra +1 (Mar) -> incremental OPEX YR1: $2.1M (pro-rated)
- Slow hire (conservative): Solutions +1 contract->FTE conversion in Q3, Sales +0, Infra +0 -> incremental OPEX YR1: $180k

Unit economics sensitivity table (selected slices):
- Price change vs conversion delta (immediate effect on marginal ARPU):
  * -10% price -> conversion +6% (elasticity ≈ -0.6) -> net revenue change = -4.8% unless offset by higher commit sizes
  * +10% price -> conversion -3% (inelastic at high tiers) -> net revenue change = +6.7%
- Commitment term effect: moving from monthly to 12-month reduces churn by ~30% in cohort model -> LTV uplift ~+45%

Break-even analysis (for hiring 6 solutions + 2 sales):
- Incremental pro-rated first-year cost = $2.1M (from hires + ramp + hiring overhead).
- Required net new committed ARR to justify hires = ~$3.0M ARR at target margins (assuming 72% gross margin).
- Sensitivity: if conversion drops 30% below model, required ARR > $4.2M -> hire deferral recommended.

Channel & product levers tested: (short bullets)
- Upfront pre-pay discount vs. monthly: upfront improves cash flow but lengthens legal cycle (adds ~10–14 days to conversion).
- Trial-to-commit funnel change: 14-day trial -> 30-day pilot for 4T prospects reduces churn but increases cost to serve (solutions time).
- Add-on: quick-start deployment fee to partially offset Solutions time (one-time $20k professional services).

Recommendations (working):
1) Offer a time-limited 4T 12-month discount window targeting large ISVs; prepare a 6-hire ramp scenario if we secure 8+ qualified pre-sales opportunities by Feb 29.
2) For mid-market, prioritize 2T reserved SKU with onboarding package (low-solution-touch) and delay hiring until conversion velocity observed for 60 days.
3) Maintain hosted burst fallback policy and budget a $250k buffer for egress/burst infra in Demand Shock scenario.

Open questions / decision points:
- Tradeoffs between deeper discount vs. faster close: is sales comfortable trading 5–8% additional discount for 10–14 day faster close? (Need survey.)
- Legal SLA changes required for 12-month commitments with capacity guarantees — estimate impact on margin.
- Should we pilot contractor pool for Solutions for Q1 to keep runway flexible?

Next steps (owners & timing):
- Sales to produce list of 12 high-fit prospects by 2028-01-20 (owner: Liam).
- Solutions to draft quick-start $20k package and time-box (owner: Priya) by 2028-01-18.
- Finance to run NPV mid-point sensitivity at +/-15% conversion by 2028-01-12 (owner: Maya).

Appendix (raw slices from model):
- Snapshot: PV of 24-month cohort @ baseline conversion (12%) = $1.9M per 100 deals; @ +6% conversion = $2.3M; @ -6% = $1.6M.
- Labor ramp calendar (GANTT style): Jan 2028: hire reqs posted; Feb: interviews; Mar: start date earliest for bulk hires.

Notes to self (todo):
- Add waterfall chart in next rev showing margin delta by tier and by term length.
- Link legal template for 12m commitment to Confluence and flag renewal terms.
- Re-run model with 36-month cohort for large enterprise deals (to capture longer LTV).
